method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across the cry for justice, what fairness asks of us, the consequences of deeds, oppressive power, the fall of those who seemed secure, warnings that seek a response, the repeated promise of reckoning, prayer under violence, the language of wrath beside mercy and grace, and the restoration of justice. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that God will seize the unjust and make them a lesson to all on earth; judgment as lesson.

selected.text: They that have turned away this Day have no portion in the Book. God will soon seize them with His justice. He, verily, is the Just, the All-Wise
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that those who turned away have no portion in the Book and will be seized with justice; a representative warning.

selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that, seen with the eye of truth, all people deserve punishment save whom God wills; a necessary qualification.

selected.text: O people of the earth! Whatever you have spent in the path of God, the Truth, you shall find it preserved in the hands of the Preserver at that Gate.
selected.reason: The Báb’s Commentary on the Surah of Joseph assuring that whatever is spent in the path of God is preserved; supports the theme that no good is lost.

selected.text: Soon will the luminary of justice shine forth from the horizon of the heaven of divine providence. Then shall they find themselves in manifest error.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh promising that the luminary of justice will shine from the heaven of divine providence; hope of restoration.

selected.text: And verily it is God's mercy unto the righteous and His vengeance unto the wicked. Thus has the matter been decreed by the finger of might and power.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that the same thing is God’s mercy to the righteous and His vengeance to the wicked; a concise statement of the dual effect.

selected.text: Soon shall they who have wronged be made to drink from the cup from which they made My loved ones drink. Thy Lord, verily, is the Just, the All-Wise.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that the wrongdoers will drink from the cup from which they made His loved ones drink; consequence mirrors the deed.

selected.text: God hath seized those who oppressed Us with a mighty grasp from His presence, and will seize those who transgressed against the Mighty, the All-Wise.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that God seized those who oppressed Him and will seize those who transgressed; a representative assurance.

selected.text: Verily thy Lord hath seized him who manifested oppression and arose in tyranny, and He shall soon seize those who have denied God, the Lord of lords.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that God seized the one who arose in tyranny and will seize those who denied Him; a representative assurance.

selected.text: God created man after His own image and likeness ... but now, behaving contrarily, man has become more merciless and fearless than rapacious beasts
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that man, created in God’s image, has become more merciless than rapacious beasts; a stark image of human cruelty.

selected.text: Pray, pray that God may not punish His unfaithful servants more than this! that He may pity them! This is indeed a great punishment! Pray, again pray!
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá urging prayer that God not punish His unfaithful servants more and that He pity them; closes the petitions with mercy.

selected.text: Verily He knoweth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on earth, and He judgeth between all with justice concerning that wherein they differ.

selected.text: No good deed has been or ever will be lost - all are preserved and safeguarded in the treasury of divine knowledge, and their reward shall assuredly come.

selected.text: By reason of the loftiness of His wrath and the greatness of His displeasure, He sent forth Muhammad - peace be upon him and his family - from the innermost heart of eternity unto all nations, distinct from any similitude among the children of his kind. selected.reason: The Báb describing Muhammad as sent forth as the manifestation of God’s justice and power, then of His grace; a distinctive account of wrath and grace in revelation.

selected.text: Having affirmed this, we say: How can existence be brought into being except in accordance with acceptance and acquiescence? For the matter resolves to one of four possibilities: either compelling all to obedience, or compelling all to disobedience, or compelling some to obedience and others to disobedience, or giving each its due according to the capacities of contingent beings.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh reasoning that existence can only accord with acceptance, giving each its due according to capacity; a philosophical explanation of justice.

selected.text: He is now surrounded with far worse sufferings than those with which he surrounded me. I did not feel the pains of his fiendish persecutions, because I possessed the glad-tidings of the Kingdom, but he is afflicted with the pangs of regret and remorse as the result of his evil days. These dark days have come upon him as the consequence of his darker days of tyranny and oppression.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that his persecutor now suffers worse than he inflicted, afflicted with regret and remorse; consequence as remorse.

selected.text: Such is the state of mankind. The Truth hath not and will never overlook the oppression of the oppressors, especially in this Revelation wherein each of the tyrants hath been requited. Consider the Sultan of Rum aforetime and those who circled round him. God seized them with the grasp of the Mighty, the Powerful, for without cause he sent the people of God to the Most Great Prison.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh affirming that the Truth never overlooks oppression, citing the seizure of the Sultan of Rum who sent the people of God to the Most Great Prison; a historical example.

selected.text: Nevertheless his fire burned more intensely and his wickedness increased more and more until suddenly the hands of divine wrath seized him and his circle of officials. The Governor of the province who resides in Damascus, and the chief who rules in Beirut, as well as other officers, all became troubled. Great causes appeared and that wicked one and his like were cast out and rejected
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recounting how divine wrath seized a wicked one and his officials, troubling the governors of Damascus and Beirut; a named narrative.

selected.text: Verily Thou art most severe in punishment and most exemplary in retribution. And how many servants have possessed the east of the earth and its west, yet today none remembereth them save to curse them if they are remembered, or else Thou hast elevated their mention as though they had no mention. Thus dost Thou cause the Tree of Negation to perish, even as Thou hast promised unto Thyself
selected.reason: The Báb on those who possessed the east and west of the earth and are now remembered only with curses; the fall of the powerful.

selected.text: I inform you, O servants of God, of Our severe grasp upon mankind on the Day of Judgment. Whoso turneth away from God's Remembrance, adorning falsehood with vain delusions -- by the Lord of heaven and earth, We shall make him taste on the Day of Resurrection, according to the decree of the Book, fire upon fire from the tree of fire in the depths of the coffin, as hath been ordained in the Mother Book
selected.reason: The Báb’s Commentary on the Surah of Joseph describing the severe grasp on the Day of Judgment upon those who turn away from the Remembrance; the most vivid fire passage.

selected.text: How long, O my God, wilt Thou leave the oppressed to be toyed with by the hands of the oppressors? How long, O my God, wilt Thou grant respite to the murderers and not take vengeance for the murdered? How long, O my God, wilt Thou be patient with these painful events, these deadly injustices, these tragic calamities and these grievous crimes? Has not the Hour drawn nigh, to be followed by the Catastrophe?
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking how long the oppressed will be toyed with by oppressors and murderers granted respite; opens the guide with the cry for justice.

selected.text: have no power over anything, and Our decree hath been inscribed in truth, by the truth. What aileth you that ye have disbelieved in God, your Creator, besides Whom there is none other God -- He Who created you and sustained you through His bounty, and Who hath ever been, in truth, your witness? Do ye not ponder over the Qur'an in its revelation? Do ye not reflect upon the Furqan in its interpretation? Fear ye God, from Our stern grasp of truth. If ye persist in your ways and return not unto the remembrance of God, the Most High, in truth, upon truth, and soon -- God will show you in the Day of Resurrection a fire that shall encompass your souls; on that day ye shall find no helper
selected.reason: The Báb’s Commentary on the Surah of Joseph calling people to ponder the Qur’an and fear God before a fire that encompasses souls; a warning that seeks a response.

selected.text: Among these is a sword against the polytheists of Arabia, as God the Exalted has said: "Slay the polytheists wherever you find them, and take them, and confine them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent and establish prayer and give alms, then let them go their way. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful." From these servants nothing is accepted except death or entering Islam
selected.reason: The Báb citing a Qur’anic verse on the sword against the polytheists of Arabia; retained in its own Islamic and textual setting as the guide notes.

selected.text: Even if Thou shouldst make all that Thou hast created and wilt create into fire wherein naught is mentioned save Thy fire, and shouldst enlarge my body to the greatest extent possible within Thy power, and cast me alone therein, and continue to inflict upon me at every moment that supreme torment which none before me can comprehend - even then I would deserve this as requital for my good deeds before Thy face.
selected.reason: The Báb’s prayer that even endless fire would be deserved as requital for His good deeds before God; a distinctive confession of humility.

selected.text: And upon such as knew not the right of those beloved Manifestations, from the billows of the Most High unto the lowest atom, and the purposed Dawning-Places, in the world to come and in this first life -- send down what beseemeth the deserts of each in Thy sight. For Thou art the Possessor of dread chastisement against such as know Thee not, and the Ordainer of unerring retribution against those who love not them that have believed in Thee and in Thy signs
selected.reason: The Báb’s visitation prayer for the first martyr among the Letters of the Living asking God to send what befits the deserts of each; justice as due measure.

selected.text: the Lord God foreseen that this human being will not let himself be saved, or has He, for reasons inscrutable to us, let him be ensnared from the begin-ning in folly and delusion?' But as the Lord God is not only the Almighty, but also the All-Merciful - for true might and power are always paired with kind-ness and goodness - and is at the same time the Just and the Avenger, we lowly creatures have to bow to His inscrutable decree and believe that the Potter in His absolute wisdom and goodness, in His justice and truth, creates, changes and completes everything to the best for the individual and for the whole
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on bowing to the inscrutable decree of a God both All-Merciful and Just, likened to a wise Potter; addresses the mystery of suffering.

selected.text: and God will take vengeance upon them through the sovereignty of His overwhelming power, and the dominion of His almightiness, and the might of His everlastingness, and the independence of His glorification, and the enjoyment of His grandeur. For He is the All-Powerful, the Mighty in Punishment, the All-Compelling, the Overwhelming, the Manifest, the All-Prevailing, the Triumphant, the All-Conquering, the Wrathful, the Avenger
selected.reason: The Báb’s visitation prayer for Mulla Husayn invoking God’s vengeance through a long litany of names of power; a distinctive devotional form.

selected.text: As for those who have fled from the Beauty of the All-Merciful, God hath rendered their deeds void and cast them into the abyss of His wrath as recompense for their actions and they were among the doers thereof. Take heed lest the denial of the deniers grieve thee, for We have found them today isolated in their unbelief, and therefore have We forbidden them from the holy shores with justice from Our presence, and verily We are just.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing those who fled the All-Merciful as cast into the abyss of wrath and forbidden the holy shores with justice; estrangement as consequence.

selected.text: Several times calamities have overtaken you, and yet ye failed utterly to take heed.  One of them was the conflagration which devoured most of the City with the flames of justice, and concerning which many poems were written, stating that no such fire had ever been witnessed.  And yet, ye waxed more heedless.  Plague, likewise, broke out, and ye still failed to give heed!  Be expectant, however, for the wrath of God is ready to overtake you
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: In brief, difficulties and trials assailed that wronged one from every side until it ended in deposition - he found no chance to act. During Istanbul's revolution, the head of the investigating committee, Arif, swallowed three bullets, the military commander was exiled to distant lands, the army general perished, and the colonel fled to Egypt and begged alms from the friends. Thus did God seize them with the grip of One mighty and powerful.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recounting the fates of the investigating committee’s members during Istanbul’s revolution; a dated narrative example.

selected.text: The meaning in Persian is this: "O Lord, make that judge content who gave the verdict for the shedding of this wanderer's blood both within and without the sanctuary of the Kaaba, while even hunting is forbidden in the sacred precinct. Yet that wretched one was so hard of heart that he made this servant's blood lawless
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explaining a Persian verse about the judge who gave the verdict for shedding a wanderer’s blood; injustice by a judge.

selected.text: Therefore, O my God, at this time do Thou chastise all Thine enemies, and the enemies of Thy Beloved, and the enemies of the Manifestations of Thyself, and the enemies of those who claim relationship to Thee … Seize them, O my God, through Thy might with a mighty seizure, for verily Thou art the All-Powerful, the Almighty. Chastise them, O my God, through Thy power with a great chastisement, for verily Thou art most severe in punishment and in retribution
selected.reason: The Báb asking God to chastise all His enemies with a mighty seizure; the full force of the petitions for retribution.

selected.text: For example, if a man does a great injustice to another in his life, then, after his death, his son will be despised for having had such a father, and in some cases the injury might also be so serious that the effect would reach to the grandson, etc., or a man may, by wrong living, fall into consumption and give that disease to his children unto the third or fourth generation. … Both physically and mentally, the sins of the fathers may be visited upon the children
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on how a great injustice or a disease brought on by wrong living may affect children and grandchildren; carries the guide’s question on generations.

selected.text: Then, he readily puts thousands upon thousands of them to the sword's blade. It takes twenty years for a person to grow to maturity and full strength, but in an instant, these people massacre tens of thousands of men and allow them to perish. How many cities are thoroughly destroyed, how many villages are reduced to heaps of dust, how much blood reddens the soil and how immense are the properties that are plundered and wrecked! And yet, there is no benefit in any of this!
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on war that massacres tens of thousands and ruins cities to no benefit; carries the guide’s attention to violence.

selected.text: He made reply: "I held command over the people, and here is the mandate of my authority." … "Hold thy peace, O denier of the Day of Judgement!" … He implored: "Is no respite possible so that I may send for my family?" … "Far from it, O disbeliever in the verses of God!" … Thereupon the keepers of the fathomless abyss called unto him: "The gates of Hell have opened wide to receive thee, O thou who hast turned away from thy Lord, the Unconstrained! Repair unto its fire, for it yearneth after thee
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: O Lord! Let Thy just servant drink from the cup of bounty and make him drunk with the wine of guidance, and make him a sword of equity unsheathed upon the necks of the people of tyranny, and a gleaming blade upon the necks of the deniers, and a cutting sword upon the necks of the proud ones. Verily Thou art the Mighty, the Powerful, the Strong, the Triumphant, the Able, the Chosen One. There is no God but Thee, the Distressed, the Sovereign, the Just, the Mighty, the Compelling.
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that a just servant become a sword of equity upon the necks of the people of tyranny; a vivid devotional image.

selected.text: Verily We shall reckon with you by God's leave on the Day of Resurrection, examining thoroughly layer upon layer, and with truth upon truth, hair by hair … And your Lord, the All-Merciful, is never in the least unjust to His servants. … If you do good, you do good for your own souls -- this is the truth that exists from God your Lord upon the paths of the Gate around the water. And if you do evil, you do it against yourselves -- this decree from you is inscribed in the Mother Book around the fire
selected.reason: The Báb’s Commentary on the Surah of Joseph describing a reckoning hair by hair and stating that good and evil are done to one’s own soul; a substantive explanation.

selected.text: At all times doth the Book of God call out and declare: "O people of the earth! The True One, glorified be His majesty, hath sent Me down from His Kingdom of utterance that ye might all hold fast unto Me and find the path of salvation. Through Me is the straight path made clear and the evident proof established. Through My being hath the world been established, through Me are mysteries revealed and lights made manifest, the ocean of knowledge billoweth and the sun of wisdom shineth resplendent
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh portraying the Book of God calling the people of the earth to the path of salvation; the invitation behind the warnings.

selected.text: In truth, the affairs that occurred in the Great City have become a cause of astonishment. People's wealth has been scattered to the wind, a great injustice has been inflicted upon justice, and the severest blow has been dealt to religion. I beseech God to protect His loved ones from the harm of those souls. Verily He has power
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on events in the Great City where wealth was scattered and a great injustice was inflicted upon justice; historical context for the warnings.

selected.text: Thou hast admitted to the Ridvan those who believe in Thy unity, having bestowed upon them glory and immortality. And Thou hast destroyed those who believe not in Thy unity and cast them into the fire for what their hands have wrought. Thy sign admits of no doubt. Who is mightier than Thee in punishment, and greater than Thee in prowess? Such is Thy punishment for him who believeth not in Thee, whom Thou cursest along with all things, even their own souls, by names before them until the Day of Resurrection.
selected.reason: The Báb’s visitation prayer for the martyrs contrasting the Ridvan of believers with the fire of deniers; the devotional setting of judgment.

selected.text: And as for me, within the bounds of my low estate, when I behold one who treadeth the path of Thy good-pleasure, how could I fail to manifest toward him the modes of mercy? For from me he hath acquired naught that would call forth My judgment upon him, but rather pardon from My presence. And when I behold one bereft of the modes of Thy love and good-pleasure, needs must I robe myself in the garment of decree and of forgiveness -- albeit this proceedeth from the repugnance of my heart and from what Thy beingness would fain not witness concerning
selected.reason: The Báb’s prayer describing mercy toward one who treads God’s path and judgment assumed with repugnance of heart; a distinctive qualification.

selected.text: The wretchedness of those who denied the Days of God, wherein the Cause dawned from the horizon of mysteries, hath prevailed. We have seized those who disbelieved in God and wronged the Dawning-Places of Revelation. Verily thy Lord is severe in punishment. Among them were those whom We seized with might from Our presence, those whom We destroyed with a single cry, those whom We drowned in the sea, those whom We caused the earth to swallow, those whom We burned with the flames of fire, and those upon whom We rained stones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh listing the forms of seizure, from a single cry to drowning and stones, upon those who wronged the Dawning-Places; a vivid catalogue.

selected.text: ye till God will have changed His favour unto you. Nothing whatsoever escapeth Him. He knoweth the secrets both of the heavens and of the earth. His knowledge embraceth all things. Rejoice not in what ye have done, or will do in the future, nor delight in the tribulation with which ye have afflicted Us, for ye are unable by such means as these to exalt your stations, were ye to examine your works with acute discernment
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Were it not for His grace and other wisdoms, verily those souls who have caused the least harm and injury to the loved ones of God would have been cast into the lowest depths of hell, and the earth would not have borne them for a moment. This applieth to the weak, heedless, and ignorant souls. As for those who arose in utter opposition and who stood against the Dawning-Places of God's love and the Daysprings of His remembrance in this Most Great Revelation with rejection and protest, they have been and shall be seized by the hand of power. Verily, thy Lord is the Avenger, the Mighty Wielder of Authority.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh distinguishing the weak and heedless, restrained by grace, from those who arose in utter opposition; a necessary qualification on degrees of guilt.

selected.text: I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thyself and by those who have ascended unto Thee through the attraction of their hearts and the severance of their bodies, to visit those who have waxed proud in the land without right and who refuse to prostrate themselves before Thee or worship Thee with Thy most severe vengeance, to destroy them with utmost speed, to afflict them with Thy most grievous punishment, and to annihilate them from the face of the earth until no mention of them remaineth except coupled with Thy curse. For this is the recompense of those who believe not in Thee, who deny Thy Messenger, and who believe not in Thy signs.
selected.reason: The Báb’s prayer asking vengeance on those who have waxed proud in the land without right; the petitions in their most severe form.

selected.text: For the general body is like the human person: since it is composed of individual elements and different, opposing, and conflicting components, it is necessarily subject to ailments and exposed to diseases. When disorders arise from various causes, the skilled physician and superior sage diagnoses the disease, proceeds to analyze the symptoms, contemplates the realities and subtleties of the cause and requirements of nature, investigates origins and results, means and needs, and distinguishes between particulars and universals. Then he considers what this illness requires and what these symptoms demand, and proceeds with treatment and cure.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá comparing the body politic to a human person whose ailments a skilled physician diagnoses before treating them; a memorable image for remedying social disorder.

selected.text: But verily, Thou, O my God, wert ever watching until Thou didst seize them. And how severe was their punishment! Thou didst send upon them a yellow, raging wind that spared nothing and left nothing, scorching all flesh. The transgressors abandoned all their homes and properties, fleeing to the wilderness in fear of the deceptive disease. They could find no rest, O my God, even in the mountain peaks, for the disease crushed them, the devastating plague destroyed them, and the torrent of illness swept them away. Thou didst punish each one a thousandfold, O my God, scattered their gatherings and dispersed their assemblies until not one could find another.
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the raging wind and plague that scattered the transgressors; a vivid image of overthrow.
